meta.title: ERE WE WERE
meta.reel: The Lost Secrets of Giza II — The Long Count

lanes.subtitle: 5239 BC to 2106 AD, folded at 1567 BC

stations.title: THE LONG COUNT
stations.claim: Breshears starts his clock 1,344 years before Year One and runs it to the capstone
stations.anchor: From 5239 BC to 2106 AD is 7,344 years, with no year zero. Divide by three: 2,448.
stations.fact: From 5239 BC to 2106 AD is 7,344 years, with no year zero. Divide by three: 2,448.
stations.check: 5239 BC is the start of Breshears’ Anunnaki reckoning (Chronicon) · 5239 + 2106 − 1 = 7,344, because there is no year zero.
stations.natori: Fifty-two thirty-nine BC. Before Year One, before the pyramid, somebody was already counting.
stations.rogue: Seven thousand three hundred forty-four years from here to the capstone. Hold on to that number.

stations.title: THE DRAGON STAR
stations.claim: The descending passage points north, at the pole star of its age: Thuban, the eye of the Dragon
stations.anchor: Thuban, Alpha Draconis, was the pole star around 2800 BC. The descending passage slopes at about 26°.
stations.fact: Thuban, Alpha Draconis, was the pole star around 2800 BC. The descending passage slopes at about 26°.
stations.check: Precession: Thuban was nearest the pole c. 2830 BC · the 3440 BC aim and the 3439 BC catastrophe are Breshears’ readings; Herschel and Piazzi Smith gave other dates.
stations.natori: Thirty-four forty BC. The passage in the north face points at the eye of the Dragon.
stations.rogue: The old pole star. When it sat in that shaft, he says, a third of the world died.

stations.title: TWO EGYPTS
stations.claim: Every pyramid in Egypt stands in the north; the kings of the Valley lie far to the south, with none
stations.anchor: Giza to the Valley of the Kings is about 500 km as the crow flies. No pyramid stands there.
stations.fact: Giza to the Valley of the Kings is about 500 km as the crow flies. No pyramid stands there.
stations.check: Straight-line distance ≈ 500 km (311 mi); the talk’s 416 miles is nearer a road route · the 1899 BC uplift is Breshears’ Chronicon.
stations.natori: Eighteen ninety-nine BC. He says the sea let go of the north, and the land rose.
stations.rogue: Two Egypts. The pyramids in one, the kings’ tombs in the other, weeks of walking apart.

stations.title: EXODUS 2448
stations.claim: Breshears’ number for a people leaving a dying world is 2,448, and the pyramid keeps returning it
stations.anchor: 2448 AM is 1447 BC on his calendar. 7,344 ÷ 3 = 2,448, and 204 years is 2,448 months.
stations.fact: 2448 AM is 1447 BC on his calendar. 7,344 ÷ 3 = 2,448, and 204 years is 2,448 months.
stations.check: 3895 − 2448 = 1447 · 1447 BC is the traditional early Exodus date (from 1 Kings 6:1); many scholars prefer the 13th century BC.
stations.natori: Fourteen forty-seven BC. Good people leave a bad world. He files it under one number.
stations.rogue: Twenty-four forty-eight. A third of the long count. Two hundred four years, counted in months.

stations.title: THE MIDDLE YEAR
stations.claim: Fold the 7,344 years in half and Breshears lands on Megiddo, the first Armageddon
stations.anchor: 5239 BC plus 3,672 years is 1567 BC. Another 3,672 reaches 2106 AD. The exact centre.
stations.fact: 5239 BC plus 3,672 years is 1567 BC. Another 3,672 reaches 2106 AD. The exact centre.
stations.check: The arithmetic holds (no year zero) · Thutmose III’s Battle of Megiddo is usually dated 1457 or 1479 BC, not 1567.
stations.natori: Fifteen sixty-seven BC. Fold the long count in half, and it creases here.
stations.rogue: Megiddo, he says. The first Armageddon, sitting dead centre of the whole run.

stations.title: THE STRIPPING
stations.claim: Earthquakes cracked the white armour; the builders of Cairo took the rest
stations.anchor: After the earthquake of 1303, casing stone was carted off to build Cairo. Sultan Hassan’s mosque is said to hold some.
stations.fact: After the earthquake of 1303, casing stone was carted off to build Cairo. Sultan Hassan’s mosque is said to hold some.
stations.check: Al-Maqrizi records the 1303 quake · the Sultan Hassan attribution is a long tradition, not a surveyed fact.
stations.natori: Thirteen oh three. The ground shook, the white skin cracked, and Cairo came for the pieces.
stations.rogue: Sixty years of hauling. What the flood could not strip, a building boom did.

stations.title: DAVISON’S CHAMBER
stations.claim: Five low rooms stacked over the King’s Chamber carry the mountain’s weight away from it
stations.anchor: Nathaniel Davison found the first relieving chamber in 1765. Vyse blasted into four more in 1837.
stations.fact: Nathaniel Davison found the first relieving chamber in 1765. Vyse blasted into four more in 1837.
stations.check: Vyse’s 1837 chambers carry the builders’ red-paint marks, including Khufu’s name, Egyptology’s key dating evidence; Breshears dates the build to 2905–2815 BC.
stations.natori: Seventeen sixty-five. A ladder, a candle, and a crawlway into a room nobody had seen.
stations.rogue: Granite beams, stacked five deep, so the chamber below never feels the weight.

stations.title: THE GUARDIAN
stations.claim: Breshears: the body is a dog’s, Anubis at the gate, and the head was recut small
stations.anchor: The Sphinx is about 73 metres long and 20 high. Baraize cleared its enclosure from 1925 to 1936.
stations.fact: The Sphinx is about 73 metres long and 20 high. Baraize cleared its enclosure from 1925 to 1936.
stations.check: Egyptology: carved for Khafre, c. 2500 BC · the Anubis reading is Breshears’ (after Robert Temple).
stations.natori: Nineteen twenty-six. They dig the sand from its paws. The head looks too small for the body.
stations.rogue: He says it was a jackal once. The riddler at the gate, keeping us out of Eden.

stations.title: THE CAPSTONE
stations.claim: Two hundred three courses stand. The last, the chief cornerstone, is missing, and he reads the gap as time
stations.anchor: 6000 AM is 2106 AD. 1,902 + 204 = 2,106, and a 612-foot face is exactly 7,344 inches.
stations.fact: 6000 AM is 2106 AD. 1,902 + 204 = 2,106, and a 612-foot face is exactly 7,344 inches.
stations.check: 6000 − 3894 = 2106 by the Chronicon rule · surveys give 201–210 courses (203 is the usual figure) and a face slope near 186 m, ≈ 611 ft.
stations.natori: Twenty-one oh six. Two hundred three courses stand. The last one is still missing.
stations.rogue: Set the capstone and the count closes. Six thousand years. Every stone, a name.
